newsitem.title: USA: No big shift seen in Japan portfolios ahead of EMU.
newsitem.headline: No big shift seen in Japan portfolios ahead of EMU.

text.p: Japanese investors and financial institutions plan no big changes in their portfolios in the run-up to the launch of European monetary union in 1999, a senior Ministry of Finance official said.

"The current stance ... is to make no fundamental change in the period to the year 1999 due to the general uncertainty involved," Takatoshi Kato, Vice Finance Minister for International affairs, said.
"However," he added, "some expect an increase in investment in euro-denominated securities if the introduction of the euro increases the liquidity of European markets."

Kato told a conference at the International Monetary Fund that Japanese investors will base their portfolio decisions on a variety of factors, including how strictly the Maastricht Treaty criteria for the launch of EMU are applied.

"In order for the introduction of the European single currency to have a positive effect on the global economy, it is essential that it be introduced in an orderly manner and without confusion," he said.
In that regard, Kato stressed the importance of the parity at which existing European currencies will be changed into euros.
That parity must be determined in a way and at a time designed to enhance the credibility of EMU in financial markets, he said.
It is also important that European nations continue their efforts to bring their economies into greater convergence after 1999, Kato added.
